chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Umar ibn Yazeed, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about the day of Friday and its night, so he said: 'Its night is luminous and its day is a day of brilliance, and there is no day upon the earth on which the sun sets that is more pardoned from the Fire than it. The one who dies on the day of Friday, recognizing the right of the People of this Household, Allah has written for him freedom from the Fire and freedom from the Punishment; and the one who dies on the night of Friday is liberated from the Fire.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: The People of this Household (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of dying on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) elevates Friday as the preeminent day of the week, characterizing its night as 'luminous' and its day as 'radiant,' a status rooted in Shia tradition as the day of the Prophet's death and the Imam's appointment. The text emphasizes that recognition of the Ahl al-Bayt's right (Haqq) serves as the key intercessory mechanism for liberation from Hellfire, linking eschatological salvation directly to theological knowledge (Ma'rifah). This underscores the Shia view that Friday is not merely a weekly ritual but a cosmic axis of divine mercy and judgment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husay, from Ali Bin Al Numan, from Umar Bin Yazeed, from Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the day of Friday and its night. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Its night is honourable and its day is a day of brilliance, and there isn’t a day upon the earth a day wherein the sun sets, more Pardoning from the Fire than it. The one who dies on the day of Friday, recognising the right of the People<sup>asws</sup> of this Household, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Write for him freedom from the Fire and freedom from the Punishment; and the one who dies on the night of Friday would be Liberated from the Fire’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu‘man from ‘Umar ibn Yazid from Jabir who has said the following: “Someone asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about Friday and its night. The Imam replied, ’Friday night is the finest; its day is brilliant. There is no other day in which sunset takes place with as many rescued from the fire as is on Friday. If one dies on Friday while fully acknowledging the rights of Ahl al-Bayt (people of this house), Allah writes for him the certificate of freedom from the fire and punishment. If one dies on a Friday night, he is set free from the fire.’”
